newsitem.title: CROATIA: Strong quake hits southern Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake hits southern Croatia.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook Croatia's Adriatic tourist coast on Thursday night, causing extensive damage and reportedly injuring one person, state radio and witnesses reported on Friday.

The tremor, measuring 6.0 on the Richter scale, hit at 10:44 p.m. (2044 GMT) and its epicentre was between the southern Adriatic resort of Dubrovnik and the town of Ston, 50 km (30 miles) to the north.

"The old town of Ston collapsed like a castle made of cards," Eduard Cengija, head of Dubrovnik police, said after inspecting the site, adding that a number of people had been evacuated from the area.

A Reuters reporter in Ston said many houses were badly damaged but only a few had collapsed. Women, children and elderly walked the streets littered with rubble and shattered glass, quietly loading their belongings on evacuation trucks.
The radio reported a girl was seriously injured in the town of Slano but doctors at Dubrovnik hospital said no one had been admitted so far.
"This area is not densely populated. Besides, it's the end of the tourist season so there are not so many people around," doctor Damjan Djuricic told Reuters.
According to a local tourist association there are currently some 5,300 tourists in Dubrovnik area, roughly half of them foreign.
Seismologists said the area was still suffering light tremors "every hour or two".
"But nothing indicates there could be another strong quake," Vlado Kuk of the Zagreb Institute for Seismology told Reuters.
State television said almost 80 percent of residential buildings in Ston were destroyed by the tremor, but no official assessment of the damage has been made yet.
The quake knocked out power and caused landslides blocking the coastal road to Dubrovnik and the road was later reopened to traffic.

The tremor was also felt on the Dalmatian islands of Brac and Hvar to the north and inland at Imotski and Sinj, the radio said. The state news agency HINA said a number of people were injured in Ravno, in nearby southern Bosnia.
The tremor could be felt hundreds of kilometres (miles) to the north in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.

No damage was reported in Dubrovnik, a famous mediaeval town dubbed "the pearl of the Adriatic" although frightened residents rushed out of apartment buildings and gathered on the streets after the quake struck.
"Dubrovnik has suffered practically no damage. Life goes on as usual and there is no need for tourists to leave the town," Lucija Curic of Dubrovnik's tourist association told Reuters.
